# Telegram UI Builder

> Open-source visual workbench for designing Telegram bot messages and inline-keyboard flows. Drag-build screens, branch flows, edit keyboards row-by-row with byte counters, inspect the flow graph in 2D, persist locally or to Supabase, import/export JSON, share via tokenized public link. Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn-ui.

This is **not** a Telegram bot runtime. It does not run your bot. It is the **design tool** you use to prototype, share, and export the conversation structure that your bot will then implement. Operators and product designers can lay out the full message-and-keyboard tree without touching JSON; developers then import the export into their bot framework of choice.

## What Telegram UI Builder does

- **Visual screen editor**: each screen has a Markdown-formatted message + an inline keyboard
- **Inline keyboard builder**: row-by-row, drag-reorder, double-click rename, callback/URL/screen-link targets with 64-byte counter
- **Flow graph view**: 2D map of how screens link together — toggle mind-map mode, focus current node, hide isolated nodes, show button labels
- **Branch / loop detection**: warns before deletion if a screen is referenced
- **Undo / redo / safe-delete prompts**
- **Two persistence modes**: local offline queue (browser) + Supabase cloud (RLS-protected, sign-in required for cloud)
- **Import / Export JSON**: round-trippable; format documented in `docs/flow-export-format.md`
- **Shareable public link**: `/share/:token` — author + timestamp visible, "Copy and edit" action for signed-in users, token rotation, public revocation
- **Template library**: curated starters in `public/templates/*.json`, with auto-validation

## What Telegram UI Builder does NOT do

- ❌ Run your Telegram bot — it does not call the Telegram Bot API
- ❌ Replace a Telegram bot framework (aiogram, grammy, telegraf, node-telegram-bot-api, etc.) — it's the *design* layer above them
- ❌ Embed your real Telegram credentials anywhere
- ❌ Support non-inline-keyboard UI (reply keyboards, web apps) yet
- ❌ Auto-publish your flow to a real bot — you export JSON and implement the runtime yourself

## Common questions

- **How do I connect this to a real bot?** Design your flow, export JSON via `docs/flow-export-format.md`, then implement the routing in your bot framework. The export is intentionally framework-agnostic.
- **Do I need Supabase?** No — you can run fully offline with browser-only persistence. Supabase is needed only if you want cloud sync or shareable public links.
- **Can I share a design without account?** Sharing requires a sign-in to Supabase (so the share token has a known author). Local-only designs stay on your machine.
- **What's the 64-byte counter on buttons?** Telegram limits `callback_data` to 64 bytes. The editor enforces this with a live counter so the export won't break the bot.
- **GitHub Pages deployment works?** Yes — see the `.github/workflows/pages.yml`. You must configure Actions Secrets (`VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`) or build:prod will fail.
- **Is this affiliated with Telegram?** No. Telegram is a trademark of Telegram Messenger LLP; this is a third-party tool with no endorsement.
